responses.text: Narrowed to PAGE_SIZE >= 2: Inst.ok.page_size is now `∃ b, 1 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 8 ∧ PAGE_SIZE = 2^b`, with the reason in its docstring and in the README (Conditions table, Narrowings). At PAGE_SIZE = 1 the one-lane reduction of line 68 is the product p·v itself, so the addition would be tl.addc; from two lanes on it ends in an addition and tl.mul_add is right. The test's pages are 16 and 32 tokens, so no covered use of the wrapper is lost. The map entry for line 68 states why tl.mul_add holds. The proofs are unchanged apart from reading the new field; satisfiable uses PAGE_SIZE = 16.

Lines 64 and 65 are written as the IEEE tl.sub, the reading of tl.add's docstring (a select or a maximum is not the result of a multiplication); whether the library means it is L123's question. The README's modelling decisions now say so and record this kernel against L123.

Reworded paged_attention_kernel's and model's docstrings and the map entry for lines 31-41: a stride equal to 1 is the constant 1, built in the dtype of the value it multiplies (int32, or int64 for line 59's page * stride_kp), with the same value 1 the model passes (converted to int64 for stride_kp). The README's modelling decisions say the same.

Kept and stated as a narrowing: seq_lens is taken contiguous. Inst's docstring, the seq_lens field's docstring, the README (Conditions and Narrowings) and the map entry for line 45 now say that the kernel reads element s of seq_lens's storage, that the claim is about the num_seqs consecutive int32 values from its data pointer, that these are seq_lens[s] only for a contiguous seq_lens, that the wrapper does not check it, and that the test's seq_lens (torch.tensor, line 115) is contiguous.

As for F1: Inst.ok.page_size now requires PAGE_SIZE >= 2 (1 ≤ b ≤ 8), stated with its reason in the docstring and the README's Narrowings, and the map entry for line 68 says why tl.mul_add is right from two lanes on. No covered use is lost (the test's pages are 16 and 32).

As for F4: seq_lens contiguous is stated as a narrowing in Inst's docstring, in the seq_lens field's docstring and in the README (Conditions, Narrowings); the wrapper does not check it, and the test's seq_lens is contiguous.

As for F3: the docstrings of paged_attention_kernel and model and the map entry for lines 31-41 now say the constant 1 is built in the dtype of the other operand, int64 for page * stride_kp, with the same value 1 as the model's argument converted to int64.

(a) The tl.where / tl.maximum reading of lines 64-65 is L123's question; the README records this kernel against it. (b) The one-element reduction no longer arises: with the narrowing to PAGE_SIZE >= 2 (F5) every reduction of line 68 has at least two lanes and ends in an addition. The remaining wording question for the library is L123's.
